item.title: Only Tk 5.61b disbursed to reopen closed factories, despite Tk 200b allocation
item.description:
Only Tk 5.6 billion (Tk 561 crore) has been disbursed from the incentive fund established by Bangladesh Bank to reopen closed industrial factories.

A further Tk 9.295 billion (Tk 929.5 crore) is being processed for disbursement under the scheme. The fund has an allocation of Tk 200 billion (Tk 20,000 crore). Over the past five months, industrial entrepreneurs have received less than 3 per cent of the allocated amount.

Around five months ago, Bangladesh Bank announced an incentive package worth Tk 600 billion (Tk 60,000 crore) to stimulate the economy as a whole. The package was subsequently increased to Tk 620 billion (Tk 62,000 crore). During these five months, less than one-fifth, or 20 per cent of the total incentive funds could be disbursed. As of 15 October, approximately Tk 119.60 billion (Tk 11,960 crore) had been released.

Bangladesh Bank stated this in a press release issued today.

According to a press release issued by Bangladesh Bank, a total of Tk 119.598 billion (Tk 11,959.82 crore) had been disbursed under 15 pre-financing and refinancing schemes included in the incentive package as of 15 October. Financing worth a further Tk 25.6 billion (Tk 2,560 crore) is being processed.

The total amount disbursed and under processing stands at approximately Tk 145.198 billion (Tk 14,519.79 crore).

How much has been disbursed in each sector?

According to Bangladesh Bank’s statement, cumulative disbursements under the various schemes include Tk 69.17  billion (Tk 6,917 crore) under the pre-shipment credit refinancing scheme. Another Tk 25 billion (Tk 2,500 crore) has been disbursed under a special scheme to support cottage and small enterprises, while approximately Tk 9.08 billion (Tk 908 crore) has been disbursed from the working capital refinancing fund for the cottage, micro, small and medium enterprise (CMSME) sector.

In addition, Tk 5.61 billion (Tk 561 crore) has been disbursed under the pre-financing scheme supporting closed industrial and service-sector enterprises. A further Tk 92.95 billion (Tk 929.5 crore) in financing for this sector is being processed. The scheme established to support the creative economy has disbursed Tk 5 billion (Tk 500 crore), while Tk 2.93 billion (Tk 293 crore) has been disbursed under the refinancing scheme aimed at increasing agricultural production, expanding economic activities in rural areas, ensuring food security and creating employment.

Bangladesh Bank said Tk 2 billion (Tk 200 crore) had been disbursed under the financing scheme for creating overseas employment opportunities, Tk 486.7 million (Tk 48.67 crore) under the refinancing scheme to establish a special agriculture-based economic zone in northern Bangladesh, and Tk 325.9 million (Tk 32.59 crore) under the startup financing scheme. A further Tk 50 million (Tk 5 crore) is being processed under the startup scheme.

Meanwhile, financing worth Tk 10 billion (Tk 1,000 crore) under the scheme for creating employment opportunities for unemployed young people, Tk 5.27 billion (Tk 527 crore) under the refinancing scheme for green factory buildings and green industries, and  Tk 980 million (Tk 98 crore) under the financing scheme for export-oriented leather goods and footwear businesses is being processed.

Incentive package fails to gain momentum

Bangladesh Bank announced an incentive fund of Tk 620 billion (Tk 62,000 crore) to revive the economy, including reopening closed factories. Loans from the fund are supposed to be offered to industrial entrepreneurs at an interest rate of no more than 7 per cent. The government will cover the remaining 6 percentage points of interest.

The package also set a target of creating employment for 2.5 million people. However, five months after the incentive package was announced, loan disbursements have yet to gain the expected momentum. Industry insiders say factories are not benefiting from the initiative as intended. Instead, industrial enterprises are struggling with multiple challenges, including fuel shortages.

item.title: ILLIYEEN’S CoolTech: Rethinking luxury through fabric technology
item.description:
When we think of luxurious clothing, we always envision opulent, rich shades, the latest trends, and a hefty price tag.

More often than not, an overlooked feature of what makes an item of clothing truly luxurious is the material itself. How it feels on the skin, the way it drapes, and how well it holds up through the day. After all, everyone wants their money’s worth.

Fabric innovation has made long strides globally. Bangladesh isn’t far behind either. A headliner in this conversation is the luxury brand ILLIYEEN, the high-end retailer, who has been developing fabrics that focus on both craftsmanship and functional ease, reports a press release.

Consider our current weather. We are stepping into autumn, but the days tell a mixed story. Mornings still bring that familiar, lingering heat. You step outside, and the humidity catches you off guard. By late afternoon, the sun eases up, and a softer breeze sets in. Then, out of nowhere, an unexpected shower drenches the streets, and the humidity settles back in.

Navigating this unpredictable transition isn't easy. You need attire that adapts without forcing you to compromise on style and comfort. That is where ILLIYEEN’s CoolTech innovation comes in.

CoolTech is a fabric technology engineered for our local climate. The secret lies in its specialised weave structure, and it’s not just about lightweight threads. It begins at the first touch: the instant coolness felt the moment the fabric meets the skin, with a smooth, soft feel that is easy to live in all day.

Superior moisture management then works for temperature regulation, so that first impression carries through the hours that follow. Beyond temperature regulation, there is no stiffness or rough friction, just a gentle, supple softness that lasts all day.

Then comes the drape. True luxury should never feel rigid or heavy. CoolTech falls naturally, moving effortlessly with your body. ILLIYEEN’s thobes made with CoolTech fabric stay refined and crease-resistant, a rare feat for garments made with long swaths of fabric.

Real luxury does not need to be loud. It speaks for itself in superior craftsmanship, high-grade materials, and precision tailoring rather than just a high price tag or a visible logo.

item.title: State Minister Ishraque explains why he took part in anti-narcotics raid with firearms
item.description:
Ishraque Hossain, State Minister for Liberation War Affairs, has explained his participation in an anti-narcotics operation in Gandaria, in the capital, and his decision to carry a firearm.

He said he had visited the area on Saturday as part of a coordinated social resistance initiative against drugs, involving local residents and law enforcement agencies. According to him, the operation was a joint undertaking agreed upon by police, local politicians and community leaders. He said he had raised the firearm in self-defence.

The incident took place near Gandaria Railway Station in Dhaka-6 constituency on Saturday afternoon. A video of the incident was posted on the Facebook page of Ishraque, the Member of Parliament for the constituency, and quickly went viral, prompting widespread discussion and criticism.

Several media outlets subsequently reported on the incident. On Sunday afternoon, Ishraque issued a statement on his verified Facebook page explaining his position.

The video of the anti-narcotics operation posted on Ishraque Hossain’s Facebook page had the image of the pistol blurred. However, the firearm was clearly visible in some sections of the footage.

According to the statement, since assuming office as the elected representative for Dhaka-6, Ishraque had received repeated complaints about drug dealing in Ghantighar, Munshitek, Koratitola and surrounding areas of Gandaria.

According to the statement, local residents had also raised specific concerns with him about the spread of drug use among students at educational institutions. In the aftermath of the 2024 mass uprising, the area had become one of the principal transit points for drug syndicates, the statement claimed.

Following a drug-related violent incident in June, in which three innocent civilians were shot and wounded, Ishraque visited the area and held several coordination meetings with senior law enforcement officials. He also sent a demi-official (DO) letter to the relevant police station requesting measures to address the shortage of personnel and establish a permanent police outpost near the drug dens. The proposal, however, remains under consideration for implementation.

The statement further said that, most recently, Ishraque had visited the area as part of a coordinated social resistance initiative involving members of the public and law enforcement agencies, following a joint decision by police, local political figures and community leaders.

According to the statement, before the visit, Ishraque had been warned by law enforcement agencies and his own intelligence sources of potential security threats, including the possibility of sudden gunfire from rooftops by drug dealers.

During the operation, as the group approached a makeshift drug den, between 30 and 35 alleged lawbreakers suddenly began shouting and advanced aggressively towards their motorcade, the statement claimed.

In the statement, Ishraque said, “Under these circumstances, in view of the specific threat of an attack and the need to protect lives and property, I and my government security personnel got out of the vehicles and raised our firearms in self-defence for a very brief period. As soon as the potential threat of an untoward incident had passed, the firearm was immediately put away. The firearm in question is duly licensed by the competent authority, and its display was undertaken solely for the purpose of self-defence and within the framework of the law.”

The statement added that Gandaria police station was informed shortly after the group arrived at the scene. Subsequently, joint operations were conducted at suspected drug dens in the direct presence of, and with assistance from, the police.

During the operation, four to five illegal and makeshift drug dens were dismantled. Heroin or heroin-like narcotics, foreign liquor, drug-use paraphernalia, several locally made sharp weapons, cash believed to have been generated from drug sales, and mobile phones reported to have been snatched were seized from the sites.

Six suspected drug dealers were detained in connection with the offences and handed over to Gandaria police, along with the seized evidence, the statement said.

In his statement, Ishraque said that a handful of media outlets, including Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, The Daily Ittefaq and Daily Kalbela, had unfortunately published misinformation and distorted reports based on incomplete information and photo cards, driven by what he described as excessive zeal.

He alleged that these distorted, false and entirely fabricated reports had deliberately overlooked the operation’s achievements, the role of the police, the recovery of drugs and weapons, and the detention of six offenders. He further accused the outlets of attempting to mislead both the government and the public.

According to Ishraque, the outlets had focused exclusively on the isolated image of a “state minister conducting a raid with a firearm”, promoting it through sensational headlines—a practice he said was contrary to the principles of independent and objective journalism.

He added that videos, photo cards and headlines focusing on a few seconds of a sensitive incident cannot assess the wider context. He alleged that such coverage was an attempt to deliberately create public confusion about his role and intentions.

Ishraque urged the media to verify the accuracy of reports and publish them with their full context.

The state minister also reiterated the government’s “zero-tolerance” policy towards drugs. He said that completely dismantling drug dens and making Dhaka-6 free of drugs were among his principal commitments to the public.

He maintained that the social movement taking shape against drugs would not be brought to a halt by the selective and allegedly deliberate portrayal of a single incident. The operation, he said, would continue in the public interest.

item.title: The concert for 1.5 million people and the unfulfilled dream of Ayub Bachchu
item.description:
Ayub Bachchu had a dream once. He wanted to stand before 1.5 million people with a guitar in his hands. Famous local and foreign musicians would share the stage with him. The crowd would lose themselves in the music and magic of his guitar.

The legend of Bangladeshi band music dreamed of holding this mega concert at Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka. He had another dream to host a competition for young guitar players. He also dreamed of building a guitar school for new learners for them to practice and build their skills.

None of these dreams came true. On 18 October 2018, Ayub Bachchu's journey came to a sudden halt. Eight years have passed since then. Today, his dreams still remain. So do his guitars.

Ayub Bachchu would have been 64 years old if he was alive today. Maybe he would have given us many more great songs. Maybe he would have handed guitars to new artistes. Or maybe he would be playing on the stage of that dream concert on an autumn evening.

But we will never know how his presence would have shaped Bangladesh’s band music today. How he would work with the new generation. But his incomplete dreams remind us of this one truth that Ayub Bachchu never made music just for himself. He always wanted to do something much bigger for music.

A special dream with guitars

To Ayub Bachchu, the guitar was not just an instrument. It was the biggest part of his life. Walking onto the stage with a guitar, sharing his feelings through music and cheering up the crowd—this became his true identity.

Music lovers at home and abroad knew him as a guitar wizard. But Ayub Bachchu did not just want to impress audiences. He also thought about nurturing a new generation of guitarists.

Bachchu wanted to hold a competition for fresh guitarists. His plan was to gift winners instruments from his own prized collection. The very guitars he had rocked stages with for years would one day be handed over to fresh talents. However, due to a lack of required sponsorship and support, the plan was never carried out.

In the same way, Bachchu dreamed of setting up a guitar school. He wanted to teach other instruments there as well, not just guitars. His goal was to build an environment where fresh talents could learn instruments institutionally, hone their crafts and prepare themselves comprehensively to pursue music as a profession.

If Bachchu were alive today, he might have tried to make that school happen. He could use his own experience to teach young people guitar tricks, love for music and the value of daily practice. Under his care, a new group of guitarists could have grown. They could take Bengali band music forward in their own way. We will never know for sure what would have happened. But it is clear that he truly wanted to do something good for the youth.

With a guitar in front of 1.5 million people

Ayub Bachchu brought a special energy to every concert. He sang well, but his guitar playing was even more magical. On stage with a guitar, he looked like a different person. Sometimes he created a storm with his guitar strings. Sometimes his long solos took listeners to another world.

Bachchu once shared his plan for this dream concert with this reporter during a friendly chat. He wanted to arrange a huge concert at Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka. Both local and international musicians would play on the same stage. From abroad, he wanted famous American guitarists Steve Vai, Joe Satriani, and Carlos Santana. He also wanted British drummer Ian Paice. Among local artists, he wanted James, Bassbaba Sumon, and Manam Ahmed by his side.

Talking about that dream event, Bachchu had said, "We will play for about three hours. And there will be 1.5 million people in the crowd. That will be our dream concert."

When he said this, he pictured a giant stage, a sea of people and an evening filled with guitar tunes. But that concert never took place. Eight years have passed since he died. The dream of playing guitar before 1.5 million people on Manik Mia Avenue remains unfulfilled.

A long journey through tunes

Ayub Bachchu was born on 16 August 1962 in Chattogram. He loved music from his childhood. His practice started after he got his first guitar from his father. Watching Nayan Munshi play guitar on BTV made him even more interested. Then he began to teach himself. Through sheer practice and hard work, he became famous as an iconic guitarist to Bengalis all over the world. He became an inspiration to other artists too.

Early in his career, he played with several bands. Later, he joined the band 'Souls'. While working there, he built his name as a guitarist, composer, and music director. Then, on 5 April 1991, he started his own band—'Little River Band', or LRB. Later, the full form became 'Love Runs Blind'. His time with LRB is a golden chapter in the history of Bengali band music.

Songs like Shei Tumi, Cholo Bodle Jai, Koshto Pete Bhalobashi, Rupali Guitar, Ferari Mon, and Ekhon Onek Raat are still loved by listeners today. His guitar playing mixed the power of rock, the sadness of blues, and the sweetness of melody. He made the guitar speak like a human voice, not just an accompanying instrument.

Bachchu's music does not belong to just one generation. Today's youth still listen to his songs, sing them, and experiment with them. If he were alive today, he might have worked with these young artists. He could learn new styles from them and share the stage with them. His experience and their new ideas could have created wonderful new music.

Will the guitars only remain as memories

After Bachchu passed away, many people talked about his guitar collection. Every guitar is connected to a part of his life. He played some of them on big stages. He used some to create popular tunes. Others were simply part of his private collection.

But just keeping the guitars safe is not enough. We also need to fulfill his dreams. If he were alive, he might have opened the guitar school. He would use his own guitars to teach new students. Exhibitions could be arranged with his guitars. That way, the new generation could learn an important part of band music history.

A museum could be built with his guitars, song notebooks, stage clothes, and other items. Also, a digital archive with his live videos, interviews, and music documents would be a great gift for future generations.

A Prothom Alo report earlier mentioned a government plan to save 272 songs of Ayub Bachchu and create a digital archive. Such efforts must continue. That way, people can easily find his work and future generations can learn from it. Long-term plans to keep his music alive are the best tribute to him, far better than just holding memorial events on his death anniversary.

Dreams remain, tunes live on

Eight years after his death, people in the music world still talk about Ayub Bachchu. With time, the power of his music is only growing. He may not be here to sing, but the younger generation sings his songs on many stages. Young musicians remember him with deep respect. They get inspiration from his work every day.

Musician Shuvo once told Prothom Alo about a misunderstanding he had with Bachchu. They met at an airport five days before Bachchu died, but they could not clear it up. Shuvo still feels sad about that. He said, "He had a huge impact on my whole music life. Hearing even one word from him felt like a blessing."

In 2026, Ayub Bachchu was awarded the Ekushey Padak posthumously. His wife, Ferdous Akhtar Chandana, told Prothom Alo, "Bachchu would have been very happy if he were here today. He would love to take this award with his own hands."

If Ayub Bachchu were alive today, he would smile with the Ekushey Padak in his hand. He would plan new songs. He would talk about performing before 1.5 million people again. Maybe at his guitar school, a young kid would touch guitar strings for the first time.

Maybe one of his guitars would go to a talented young artist. Or maybe, standing on stage with the new generation, he would make history with his guitar once more.

item.title: Gazipur BRT idle for 14 years as govt weighs four options
item.description:
The Dhaka-Gazipur Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project remains idle 14 years after approval, with its estimated cost now at Tk4,268 crore.
The government is preparing to present four options to the cabinet.
The options are to complete the BRT, run route-based buses on the existing infrastructure, convert the corridor into a toll expressway, or demolish the structures to build a six-lane highway.
Earlier, Roads Transport and Highways Division (RTHD) Secretary Ziaul Haque said transport experts and urban planners, along with residents and transport operators, recommended the options. They have been presented to the prime minister and will go to the cabinet.
Eventually, Mohammad Nurul Amin Khan, managing director of the BRT company, confirmed that the four options are under consideration.
Sachetan Nagarik Samaj of Gazipur held a press conference at the Dhaka Reporters Unity on Saturday, demanding the swift launch of the Gazipur-Airport Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project.
Opposing any move to demolish the project after nearly 97% of the work was complete, the organization called for a clear implementation timeline, an independent technical and economic assessment, and effective use of the existing infrastructure.
The speakers urged the government to end the 14-year delay and launch bus services immediately to ease traffic congestion and reduce public suffering in Gazipur.
The 20-kilometer project was approved in 2012 at an estimated Tk2,040 crore. The cost has since more than doubled to Tk4,268.32 crore.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is providing Tk2,118.95 crore, the French development agency AFD Tk903.49 crore, and the government Tk1,245.88 crore.
It was due to be completed in December 2016. After five extensions, the deadline was moved to December 2024.
According to project documents, around 97% of infrastructure work is complete, but overall progress stands at 77.48%.
A fourth revision proposed raising the cost to Tk6,597 crore and extending the deadline to December 2029. The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec) did not approve it on July 27, 2025, stressing the need for a review by local and foreign experts.
The government canceled a tender for electric buses, and a second tender in April 2024 for 137 air-conditioned diesel buses also failed. Seven people have died in construction-related accidents, including five who were killed on August 15, 2022, when a girder collapsed on Uttara’s Jasimuddin Avenue.
Talking to the media, Road Transport, Railways and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam has previously said there is strong support for cancellation, though some believe additional spending could still yield partial benefits. A stakeholder meeting is to be held before the final decision.
Ministry sources said the interim government had decided against proceeding, but the BNP-led government has yet to take a clear position. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met representatives of both sides in August.
A four-member team from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet), led by Prof Shamsul Hoque, reviewed reports by two ministry committees. It called the project a “systemic failure” of planning and implementation, citing weak technical evaluation, design flaws, poor coordination and lack of accountability.
The team made 17 recommendations, including emphasizing commuter rail, completing unfinished pedestrian overpasses, and relocating or auctioning the stations’ escalators and lifts.
The report names no individual.
It says the feasibility and design consultants, planning officials, financiers, the project steering committee, the Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division, and the Planning Commission must be held accountable.
“It is a very poor example,” Prof Hoque confirmed to Dhaka Tribune and describing BRT as an “imposed project”.
He said experienced professionals could have been brought in from abroad.
Despite the flaws, he added, the existing flyovers, footpaths, roads and drainage can still be used.
Prof Md Hadiuzzaman of BUET has proposed introducing public transport in phases using the existing BRT lanes.
Adil Mohammad Khan, an urban planner at Jahangirnagar University, told Dhaka Tribune that the government should prioritize making the existing infrastructure operational through an integrated public transport plan. “Demolishing it would waste public investment,” he said.
Earlier, the Bangladesh Institute of Planners (BIP) has also argued for completion. It says about 3% of infrastructure work remains, that service could begin within a year with an additional Tk300 crore, and that dismantling and compensating contractors could cost more than Tk1,000 crore.
Engineer Md Shamsul Hoque, president of Gazipur Heritage and Development, claimed that demolition and rebuilding could cost around Tk4,000 crore and take four to five years. He also alleged that a powerful group in the transport sector had obstructed the project. This claim could not be independently verified.
A senior ministry official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said abandoning the project would waste much of the borrowed money.
Proceeding, the official said, would require an additional Tk3,500 crore to buy and operate buses, posing its own risk of failure.
Another ministry source, also speaking anonymously, claimed that development partners want projects executed quickly to keep lending going and meet disbursement targets.
This claim could not be independently verified. The ADB, AFD and the Economic Relations Division could not be reached for comment.
Of 25 planned stations, 15 structures have been built in the median, but none is complete. An escalator in Uttara was briefly operated but is now out of service, while machinery at other stations is rusting. Most pedestrian overpasses in the Gazipur section remain unusable.
Nearly foot-high concrete barriers separate the lane along the route and would have to be removed if the corridor is reopened. All vehicles are currently allowed on the BRT lane. Md Sohel, a covered-van driver, said a trip from the airport area to Gazipur took 10 hours on a rainy day in 2022.
The project reportedly began before a full feasibility study and detailed design were completed. Construction revealed no proper drainage, causing waterlogging, and no plan to relocate utility lines or maintain traffic. Experts say BRT is usually built on roads with 12 to 14 lanes, whereas the Gazipur road has four and the airport section six.
The central question remains whether bus services can be launched quickly and safely on the existing infrastructure, or whether the project must be rebuilt.

item.title: Bangladesh seeks details from Saudi Arabia over executions
item.description:
Bangladesh on Sunday sought further information from Saudi Arabia regarding the recent execution of two Bangladeshi nationals, raising the issue with Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah Zafer bin Abiyah.
Foreign Secretary (East & West) Dr Md Nazrul Islam sought detailed information about the executions during a meeting with the Saudi Ambassador, a senior official at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said.
When asked whether it can be termed as summon another official said “No, it was not summon.”
Although Dhaka raised the issue with the Saudi envoy, it expressed confidence that the incident would not affect the strong bilateral relations between the two countries.
The importance of staying “mindful” of the laws of the host country was also discussed.
Both sides expressed satisfaction with the steady progress of cooperation between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia across various sectors.
On Saturday, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said the government had yet to receive detailed official information from Saudi authorities regarding the execution of a Bangladeshi man and a woman, adding that such unfortunate news was unexpected.
“We have yet to receive any official detailed information from the Saudi government,” she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, noting that Bangladesh sent a letter to the Saudi government requesting detailed information.
Earlier, Saudi media reported that the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia executed the two Bangladeshis after they were convicted of committing “indecent acts” inside a mosque in the holy city of Mecca.
Quoting the Saudi Interior Ministry, Gulf News reported that the court imposed the sentences because of the seriousness of the offence, the violation of the sanctity of the mosque, and the circumstances in which the acts were committed.
The Saudi authorities identified the two Bangladeshis as Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siti Akhtar.
“On October 14, we learned that two Bangladeshi nationals had been sentenced to death under Saudi Arabian law and that the executions had been carried out,” the state minister said, noting that neither the Ministry of Foreign Affairs nor the Bangladesh Mission in Saudi Arabia had been informed in advance.
“We wanted to know whatever we needed to know. Let the reply come. I will be able to let you know,” Shama said.
Upon learning of the incident, the Bangladesh Mission notified the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, sharing all the information it had gathered from Saudi authorities.
The state minister said the government sent a formal inquiry to ascertain the full details, including the identities of the individuals, their backgrounds in Bangladesh, and when they had originally arrived in Saudi Arabia for work.
Based on past experience, the state minister said Saudi Arabia has its own legal framework and that anyone found guilty of a grave offence is punished in accordance with the country’s laws.
“The execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia serves as a major lesson for us,” she said.
Shama Obaid said the repatriation of the bodies could be arranged once a response to the letter is received from Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Bangladesh, Uzbekistan discuss FTA to boost trade, investment ties
item.description:
Bangladesh and Uzbekistan discussed a free trade agreement on Sunday to boost trade and investment between the two countries.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir received Deputy Foreign Minister of Uzbekistan Aloyev Bakhromjon Juraboyevich in Baghdad on the sidelines of the 52nd OIC Council of Foreign Ministers and discussed the issues of mutual interest.
The two sides discussed advancing bilateral cooperation in diverse sectors, including cooperation in trade and investment, air connectivity, tourism, reciprocal support in multilateral fora and enhancing business-to-business contacts.
The state minister is leading the Bangladesh delegation to the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Baghdad taking place from Saturday to Sunday.
On Saturday, he delivered his statement in the plenary session of the Council and called for a stronger, modernised and dynamic OIC to address the challenges facing the entire Muslim Ummah.
State Minister Kobir on Saturday suggested restructuring the D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation (Developing-8) and undertaking more result-oriented activities to make the organization more meaningful.
He met D-8 Secretary General Sohail Mahmood on the sidelines of the 52nd OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad and discussed issues of mutual interest.
The state minister discussed various issues under the D-8 framework, including the promotion of intra-D-8 trade and investment, contract farming and visa waivers among member states.
The D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation is an organization for economic cooperation among Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan and Türkiye. Azerbaijan joined the organization in 2025.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh and Oman on Saturday discussed ways to explore partnerships in trade and investment, skilled migration, and the possibility of institutionalising a trade framework to advance bilateral relations beyond labour market-centric relations.
The state minister received the Under Secretary of Foreign Affairs of Oman Sheikh Khalifa bin Ali Al Harthy in Baghdad on the margin of the Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM) of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
The meeting also stressed the importance of more business-to-business and people-to-people contacts to translate existing bilateral relations into a more meaningful one.
State Minister Kobir and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Iraq Mohammed Hussein on Saturday signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) in Baghdad.
The MoUs were signed on the sidelines of the Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM) of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
The MoUs provide for the mutual exemption of visa requirements for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and for the establishment of a mechanism for regular political consultations between the two countries, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
At the signing ceremony, the two Ministers exchanged warm greetings and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the friendly and cooperative relations between Bangladesh and Iraq.
They expressed confidence that these agreements would give fresh momentum to bilateral engagement and open new avenues for cooperation in the days ahead.
Major General Md Maksudul Haque, Ambassador of Bangladesh to the Republic of Iraq, was also present.

item.title: Tarique says planning, goodwill can make areas clean, green
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday said proper planning and goodwill can make any area clean, green and beautiful, citing the visible transformation of Aminbazar over the past two months as an example.
“With proper planning and goodwill, an area can beautifully be transformed for the welfare and benefit of people. This place is the biggest proof of that,” he said.
The prime minister made the remarks after inaugurating a greening and beautification program along both sides of the Dhaka-Aricha highway by planting a sapling at Aminbazar while returning to Dhaka from Savar Cantonment.
He said the area has changed significantly over the past two months, creating a better environment for people living within around four kilometres of the site and making it easier for them to breathe cleaner air.
Tarique Rahman thanked Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanom and the officials and employees of the Local Government Ministry involved in the initiative for their efforts in transforming the area.
He urged local residents to help preserve the improved environment, saying the government has developed the area, but maintaining its beauty is now also the responsibility of the people living nearby.
“Local people must take responsibility for preserving the environmental improvements. With public cooperation alongside government initiatives, pollution and waste management problems can be gradually addressed,” the prime minister said.
He asked the DC to expand the greening program to other areas under Dhaka district near Aminbazar.
Tarique Rahman also suggested discussing with owners of mills and factories along the highway the possibility of assigning them responsibility for maintaining specific stretches.
The authorities concerned should also develop plans, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, to improve and beautify areas where waste still accumulates, he said.
The prime minister called on local lawmakers to cooperate with the district administration, expressing hope that coordinated efforts by public representatives and officials will gradually resolve waste management and environmental problems.
“Everyone must work together so that people can breathe fresh air and enjoy the beauty of nature,” he said.
Tarique Rahman said the Dhaka DC has set an example for the administration in other districts through the environmental improvement and beautification work at Aminbazar.
He expressed hope that DCs of other districts will take effective steps to transform similar areas into clean, green and attractive places.
BNP Standing Committee member and local MP Amanullah Aman, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, and State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku were present.
Earlier in the day, the prime minister attended a ceremony at Savar Cantonment to present National Standard to several battalions and regiments of the Bangladesh Army.

item.title: DB: Ishraque’s display of arms during anti-drug drive to be investigated
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) will take necessary action after reviewing the viral video showing State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain carrying a firearm during an anti-drug drive in the capital, said Additional Police Commissioner of the Detective Branch (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam on Sunday.
“It is not the right time to comment on the incident before assessing it. The deputy commissioner concerned will review the entire matter and submit a report. If any violation of law is found in the report, the DMP will take legal action,” he said at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre.
Asked whether a minister could perform duties similar to those of police during an operation, the DB chief declined to make any comment.
Earlier, a video of the drive was posted on Ishraque Hossain’s official Facebook page on Saturday afternoon.
The video shows him getting out of a vehicle with a loudspeaker and a pistol and then chasing a group of people during an anti-drug drive near the railway line in the capital’s Gandaria area.
At one point, he was seen pointing the weapon towards some people while shouting, “Hey, stop, stop.”
Another man in plainclothes was also seen chasing people with a weapon in his hand.
In another Facebook post on Saturday evening, Ishraque pledged to continue the drives until Dhaka-6 constituency is made free of drugs.
The state minister and Dhaka-6 MP, in a statement on Sunday, said he briefly raised his licensed firearm in “self-defence” during an anti-drug drive in the capital’s Gendaria area on Saturday after receiving warnings of possible “security threats”.
Ishraque said he, along with his security personnel, got out of their vehicles and raised the weapon briefly when a group of 30 to 35 people allegedly approached their convoy aggressively near a suspected drug den.
He claimed that law enforcement agencies and his own intelligence sources had warned him of possible security risks, including the possibility of drug traders firing at them from rooftops.
“The weapon was raised for a very short time in self-defence to protect lives and property amid fears of an imminent attack,” the state minister said, adding that it was put away as soon as the potential threat had passed.

item.title: Prime accused in Satkhira mob killing case arrested
item.description:
The Special Response Battalion (SRB-6) has arrested Fazlul Haque Amini, the prime accused in the murder of Wahiduzzaman Shamim in Debhata, Satkhira, following allegations of religious defamation.
SRB-6 Commander Lt Col Nistar Ahmed confirmed the matter.
Additional Superintendent of Police Zayen Uddin Muhammad Ziad, commander of SRB-6 Satkhira CPC-1, said an SRB-6 team arrested Amini, 45, during a raid in Bishnupur area of Kaliganj around 11:00pm on Friday based on a tip-off.
Amini, son of Qari Ruhul Amin of South Parulia in Debhata, was later handed over to Debhata police for further legal action.
According to the case statement, an audio recording of a conversation between Shamim, 38, and his wife was circulated on Facebook on October 12. After allegations that the recording contained derogatory remarks about religion, locals became agitated and attacked Shamim’s house.
The following afternoon, Shamim was allegedly dragged out of a rural doctor’s chamber at a local market and beaten while receiving treatment.
Police rescued him and admitted him to Debhata Upazila Health Complex. Later that night, around 8:30pm, a group allegedly led by Fazlul Haque Amini attacked the hospital, took Shamim away and assaulted him again.
Shamim died while being taken to Satkhira Medical College Hospital.
His elder brother Abdul Jalil later filed a murder case with Debhata Police Station, naming 10 people and accusing 200–250 unidentified individuals. Amini was named the prime accused.

item.title: Ex air force chief Sheikh Abdul Hannan arrested in Qatar
item.description:
Former Bangladesh Air Force chief Air Chief Marshal Sheikh Abdul Hannan has reportedly been arrested in Qatar in connection with corruption and money laundering cases, the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) said on Sunday.
Qatari law enforcement authorities arrested him on Thursday, ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan told journalists at a briefing on Sunday afternoon.
The International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) informed the ACC of the arrest by email. However, details of where and under what circumstances he was arrested, and whether steps had been taken to bring him back to Bangladesh, were not available.
In July 2025, the ACC filed 2 separate cases against Sheikh Abdul Hannan and his wife, Tahmida Begum, over allegations of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income and money laundering.
According to the case statement filed by the ACC, Sheikh Abdul Hannan acquired assets worth Tk3 crore 28 lakh 51 thousand 506 beyond his legitimate sources of income. He was also accused of suspicious transactions totaling Tk27 crore 63 lakh 66 thousand 701 through 6 bank accounts operated in his name.
Cases were filed against him under the relevant provisions of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, Money Laundering Prevention Act and Prevention of Corruption Act.
In a separate case, the ACC accused Tahmida Begum of acquiring assets worth Tk1 crore 91 lakh 90 thousand 304 beyond her known sources of income. The case statement also cited suspicious transactions of approximately Tk1 crore 18 lakh through 32 bank accounts in her name.
Tahmida Begum was named the prime accused in that case, while Sheikh Abdul Hannan was also accused of assisting his wife in acquiring illegal assets.
Earlier, courts issued several orders concerning the assets and bank accounts of Sheikh Abdul Hannan and his family members in connection with the corruption allegations.
Most recently, on September 20, a court ordered the seizure of 34 decimals of land registered in his name following an application by the ACC.
Following his reported arrest in Qatar, it remains unclear what steps the relevant authorities will take to bring him back to Bangladesh.

item.title: AG: Initiative taken to expedite hearings in Abrar, 2 other murder cases
item.description:
Attorney General Ruhul Quddus Kazal on Sunday said a special initiative is being taken to expedite hearings in three high-profile murder cases —the Narayanganj seven-murder case, retired Major Sinha Md Rashed Khan and Buet student Abrar Fahad murder cases.
The three important cases have been awaiting hearings in the Appellate Division for a long time, he said.
He said arrangements would be made for speedy hearings once court proceedings resume after the vacation.
The trials and subsequent High Court proceedings in all three cases have been completed.
Following hearings on appeals and death references, the High Court upheld death sentences and other punishments against the accused.
On April 27, 2014, seven people, including Narayanganj City Corporation councillor Nazrul Islam and lawyer Chandan Sarker, were abducted from Narayanganj court area. They were later murdered and their bodies dumped in the Shitalakkhya River.
The incident sparked widespread outrage across the country .
Following the trial court's verdict, on August 22, 2017, the High Court upheld the death sentences of 15 of the 26 convicts sentenced to death.
Retired Major Sinha Md Rashed Khan was shot dead by police at Shamlapur checkpost in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, on the night of July 31, 2020.
Following the trial court's verdict, the High Court delivered its judgment on June 2, 2025, upholding the death sentences of Pradeep Kumar Das, the then officer-in-charge of Teknaf Police Station, and Liaqat Ali, the then inspector of Baharchhara Police Investigation Centre.
The case is now awaiting a hearing in the Appellate Division.
On the night of October 6, 2019, a group of leaders and activists of Bangladesh Chhatra League beat Abrar Fahad, a second-year student of the electrical and electronics engineering (EEE) department, to death at Sher-e-Bangla Hall of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology ( Buet ).
Following hearings on appeals and death references against the trial court's verdict, the High Court delivered its judgment on March 16, 2025, upholding the death sentences of 20 convicts and life imprisonment for five others.

item.title: No DNA lab in Cox’s Bazar may delay identification of 10 fire victims
item.description:
Identifying the 10 tourists killed in a fire at Tuptup Resto & Resort in Cox’s Bazar could take up to two weeks as authorities must send DNA samples to Dhaka for testing, with no such laboratory available in the district.
The bodies are being kept at the morgue of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital pending confirmation of their identities through DNA tests at the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) forensic DNA laboratory in Dhaka.
Meanwhile, a case was filed at Ukhiya police station on Saturday night against the resort owners in connection with the fire.
A 5-member investigation committee formed by the Cox’s Bazar district administration, led by Additional District Magistrate Tasnim Jahan, visited the scene on Sunday morning.
According to sources at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital, authorities have initiated DNA testing to establish the identities of those killed in the fire at the resort. However, the absence of a DNA laboratory and the necessary equipment in Cox’s Bazar has left them dependent on the CID’s forensic DNA laboratory in Dhaka.
As most of the bodies were severely burned, their identities could not be confirmed immediately. Blood samples or buccal swabs collected from the victims’ relatives will be sent to Dhaka for comparison with samples taken from the bodies.
The bodies will be handed over to the families once the test results are available.
Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital Resident Medical Officer Dr Subuktogin Mahmud Sohel said it could take several days to send the samples to Dhaka and receive the reports. The bodies will remain preserved at the hospital morgue until their identities are confirmed.
Dr Sohel said DNA testing was the most reliable scientific method for identifying burned or disfigured bodies. He added that the CID forensic laboratory in Dhaka was the country’s primary facility for advanced forensic DNA testing.
Samples from major murder cases and accidents in different districts are also sent to Dhaka for DNA testing, he said. However, he stressed the need to establish a DNA laboratory in a major district city such as Cox’s Bazar.
Relatives of the victims have been waiting outside the morgue at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital since Sunday morning. This reporter spoke to 2 of them.
A relative named Samushuddha said 4 bodies, including that of a child, had been sent to the hospital morgue. He said he had identified the child by a bracelet on the child’s hand, while the identities of the others would be established through DNA testing.
He broke down in tears while recalling memories of the deceased.
Another relative, Ripon, said samples had been collected from 2 locations for DNA testing: the CID office in Dhaka and the bodies kept at the Cox’s Bazar morgue. Comparing the samples would allow the families to take the bodies home, he said.
Both relatives called for the DNA tests to be completed as quickly as possible so the bodies could be handed over to their families. They also demanded the establishment of a modern DNA testing laboratory in the Chittagong division or Cox’s Bazar to reduce delays in investigating major accidents and crimes.
Local residents said major accidents, fires, maritime incidents and the recovery of unidentified bodies frequently occurred in Cox’s Bazar, a major tourism destination. They said local forensic DNA testing facilities could speed up investigations, reduce difficulties and help families receive the bodies of their loved ones sooner.
The case filed at Ukhiya police station on Saturday night names the resort owners and others in connection with the fire. Those named include resort owner Tanvir Ahmad, also known as Tanvir Sultan Mia; his business partner, Niaz Morshed; resort manager Mohammad Sumon; and 1 other person.
The 5-member investigation committee formed by the Cox’s Bazar district administration, led by Additional District Magistrate Tasnim Jahan, visited the scene on Sunday morning.

item.title: IMF: Low-income countries spend up to 14% of revenue on debt servicing
item.description:
Low-income countries are having to spend anywhere from 8% to 14% of their own revenue solely on debt servicing.
These nations have come under further pressure due to rising global interest rates, high inflation, and the impact of conflicts that have driven up the prices of fuel and various commodities.
In this context, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has emphasized the need for swift and effective debt restructuring, alongside increasing concessional loans and financial support for low-income countries.
Speaking at a press conference on Saturday (October 17) on the sixth day of the IMF and World Bank Group Annual Meetings at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok, Thailand, IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva highlighted several key priorities.
Saudi Arabia's Minister of Finance, Mohammed Al-Jadaan, was also present at the event, which was moderated by Julie Kozak, director of the communications department at the IMF.
Georgieva noted that inflation and economic uncertainty make life difficult for poor people. Inflation acts much like a tax, hitting low-income populations disproportionately hard.
People want an economic environment where government policies are clear and private sectors/entrepreneurs can easily expand their businesses.
The IMF MD stated that high interest rates and inflation have made it difficult to reduce debt burdens.
Although many low-income countries have made progress in controlling debt and strengthening their financial positions, debt-servicing costs are locking up a large portion of their revenues.
According to her, while the debt-to-GDP ratio is rising in high-income nations, it has decreased somewhat in low-income countries.
However, due to high interest rates, the benefits of this ratio decrease are not being fully realized.
Georgieva rejected the notion that all low-income countries must undergo massive austerity measures or harsh economic adjustments, arguing instead that actions should be tailored to each country's economic situation and debt profile.
To expand financing opportunities for low-income countries, the IMF has taken steps to mobilize additional resources under the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT), which provides concessional loans to eligible nations.
Georgieva announced that new reforms have created the opportunity to more than triple concessional lending compared to before.
Additionally, arrangements have been made for extra financing toward capacity-development activities to enhance financial management and institutional capabilities in these countries.
Alongside financial support, she stressed the importance of boosting domestic revenue mobilization and ensuring the effective use of public funds to counter economic crises.
Underscoring the necessity of international cooperation in resolving debt crises, the IMF MD said that swift and effective action must be taken for countries requiring debt restructuring, where the G20 Common Framework can play a vital role.
Georgieva noted that while some countries have long-term debt sustainability, they face immediate liquidity shortages. Such countries need support to increase domestic revenue collection.
At the same time, an environment favorable to private investment must be created through coordinated international financing. Given that low-income nations suffer disproportionately from global economic crises and shifts, she concluded that the international community must prioritize them when providing assistance.

item.title: Near 18,500 youths from 8 districts apply to become entrepreneurs
item.description:
Under the first phase of Bangladesh Bank’s "Udyog" program—aimed at discovering young entrepreneurs at the upazila (sub-district) level and generating employment through financing—a total of 18,444 applications have been submitted across eight districts.
These applications were collected from 64 upazilas across eight districts of eight divisions between September 16 and October 15.
Application collection for all upazilas across the remaining 56 districts will begin on November 1.
Bangladesh Bank shared this information in a press release issued on Saturday.
Under the program titled "Udyog: Upazila-Level Young Entrepreneur Search, Identification, and Financing Program," interested youths submitted their applications to the designated scheduled bank branches in their respective upazilas.
According to district-wise data, the highest number of applications was submitted in Netrokona with 5,351 applications.
This was followed by Rangpur with 2,745, Naogaon with 2,456, Jhenaidah with 2,191, Habiganj with 1,552, Bhola with 1,545, Manikganj with 1,343, and Feni with 1,261.
Bangladesh Bank stated that young people in the remaining 56 districts can apply for the program from November 1 to November 30.
Applicants must fill out the prescribed form and submit it to any scheduled bank branch in their respective upazilas.
Application forms can be collected from the Bangladesh Bank website, the SME portal, and the official websites of scheduled banks.
Bangladesh Bank issued the policy guidelines for this program via a circular on September 13.
According to the guidelines, an entrepreneur can receive a maximum financing facility of up to Tk20 lakh.
This comprises a maximum loan of up to Tk10 lakh and a grant equivalent to the loan amount.
Both the loan and the grant funds will be disbursed in a single installment.
However, if the recipient fails to repay the loan, the grant portion will also be converted into a loan.
Therefore, to retain the benefit of the grant, the entrepreneur must fully repay the loan portion.
Eligible sectors under this program include agriculture, food processing, handicrafts, fisheries, livestock, tourism, services, solar power and other renewable energy, light engineering, and technology-based startups, alongside other legitimate businesses.
The objective of the program is to identify promising young entrepreneurs at the upazila level and create financing opportunities to establish new businesses and expand existing ventures.
Bangladesh Bank expects this initiative to generate new employment opportunities.
However, the final number of selected candidates and successful loan recipients following the verification of applications has not yet been determined.

item.title: Dhaka Bank holds ADB-financed Entrepreneurship Development Program in Jessore
item.description:
Dhaka Bank PLC has organized the closing and certificate distribution ceremony of its Entrepreneurship Development Program (EDP) in Jessore.
The successful initiative was carried out with the support of Bangladesh Bank under the Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program (SICIP), an initiative of the Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh.
During the event, certificates were formally awarded to 25 newly trained entrepreneurs who completed the month-long intensive program.
Additionally, 5 selected entrepreneurs were honored with crests across distinct categories: Most Innovative, Most Popular, Most Prospective, 1st Position Based on Monitoring MCQ Result and 1st Position in Overall Performance.
As part of our drive to promote digital payments, we have handed over Bangla QR codes to 25 SME entrepreneurs.
Now, customers can make quick and seamless digital transactions simply by scanning the code.
The program was chaired by Md Mostaque Ahmed, deputy managing director and chief emerging market officer of Dhaka Bank PLC.
Md Masum Billah, program director (SICIP) and additional director of the SME & Special Programs Department (SMESPD) at Bangladesh Bank, graced the occasion as chief guest.
Among others, Md Ayub Ali, deputy program director, SICIP & joint director, SME & Special Programs Department, Bangladesh Bank, Md Mahbubur Rahman Palash, head of MSME & emerging business division, Dhaka Bank, Md Humayun Kabir, manager, Dhaka Bank Jessore Branch, and AFM Mahmudur Rahman, manager, Dhaka Bank KDA Avenue Branch, Khulna along with other senior officials from Dhaka Bank, were also present.

item.title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank executes Murabaha agreement with JP Morgan
item.description:
Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC has executed a Master Murabaha Agreement with international financial institution JP Morgan to enhance the efficiency of its foreign currency liquidity management and short-term treasury operations.
Under the agreement, the bank will have the opportunity to earn overnight returns through a Shariah-compliant arrangement on foreign currency balances maintained in its nostro accounts with JP Morgan.
This initiative is expected to ensure more efficient utilization of the bank’s foreign currency balances and strengthen its short-term liquidity management.
At a ceremony held on this occasion, Sazzad Anam, executive director and head of Bangladesh Office at JP Morgan, and Mohammad Abdul Mobin, senior executive vice president and head of treasury at Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC, exchanged the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Mir Md Hassanul Zahed, executive vice president and head of financial institutions (FI), offshore and remittance business of the bank, along with senior officials from both organizations, was also present.
Through this collaboration, Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC aims to improve the efficiency of its treasury operations, optimize the utilization of its foreign currency balances, and facilitate international trade and remittance settlement activities.

item.title: Accused gets bail in headteacher’s death near Parliament House
item.description:
A Dhaka court has granted bail to Md Rakib Hossain in a case filed over the death of a school headteacher who fell from a moving autorickshaw after motorcycle-riding snatchers grabbed her bag near the National Parliament House in the capital.
Dhaka Second Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Ayesha Akter Mousumi granted his bail on a Tk5,000 bond following a hearing on Sunday.
Defence lawyer Md Mehedi Hasan Majumder confirmed the matter, saying the bail would remain effective until the police report is submitted. He expressed hope that Rakib would be released soon, as no other cases were pending against him.
The lawyer claimed that the motorcycle initially seized by police belonged to Rakib but was not used in the snatching. He said the motorcycle was at a garage at the time of the incident and that CCTV footage supported his claim. The motorcycle allegedly used in the crime was recovered later, he added.
According to the bail petition, Rakib was innocent and had been implicated in the case to harass him. It stated that the motorcycle recovered in connection with the incident did not belong to him and that no stolen items had been recovered from his possession. The petition also alleged that he had been implicated due to a media trial.
According to the case statement, the victim, Ranjila Parveen, 56, was the headteacher of Bagbari Government Primary School in Gabtali upazila of Bogra.
On August 29, she was travelling with her husband Md Abdul Matin in an autorickshaw along Manik Mia Avenue at around 5:55am when motorcycle-riding snatchers allegedly grabbed and forcefully pulled her bag near Gate No 12 of the National Parliament House. She fell onto the road and sustained severe head injuries.
She was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital and later referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, but doctors declared her dead.
Her husband subsequently filed a case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station.
On August 30, members of Rapid Action Battalion (RAB-2) arrested several suspects from different parts of the capital. They also seized a smartphone allegedly stolen during the incident, cash and a Yamaha R15 motorcycle suspected of being used in the crime. On August 31, the court granted five days of remand for the accused.

item.title: Durga Puja Maha Ashtami to be celebrated across Bangladesh on Monday
item.description:
Maha Ashtami of the six-day Sharadiya Durga Puja will be celebrated across the country on Monday with due religious fervor and festivity.
As per the puja schedule of Dhakeshwari National Temple, rituals of Maha Ashtami will be held by 7.34 am while Sandhi Puja will be held between 7.55am and 8.43am. Sandhi Puja is held at the transitional moment between Ashtami and Navami.
According to Hindu mythology, the ritual commemorates the moment Goddess Durga assumed the form of Chamunda to slay the demon brothers Chanda and Munda.
Kumari Puja, a ritual of worshipping goddess Durga in the form of a 'Kumari' - a pure-hearted girl and the virgin form of the deity, will be held at some temples as per tradition.
In the capital, Kumari Puja will be held at Ramkrishna Math and Ramkrishna Mission Dhaka at 9.30am.
During the ritual, an unmarried pre-pubescent girl, generally aged between one and 16, is worshipped as the living embodiment of the divine feminine and Goddess Durga.
Devotees offer water, clothes, flowers, and gold and silver ornaments at the feet of the Kumari during the special ritual.
Maha Saptami Puja was held this morning at temples across the country with due religious fervor. Maha Prashad was distributed among devotees after the puja.
Puja mandaps across the country came alive since last Friday with vibrant decorations, traditional Dhak beats, ringing of kashor and ghonta, conch shell blasts and ululation as the six-day grand festival began. Devotees are hopping puja pandals across the country.
A total of 33,851 puja mandaps were set up across the country this year, including 258 in the capital, according to the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad. The number of mandaps has increased by nearly 1,500 compared to last year. The Gulshan-Banani Puja Foundation is hosting one of the most elaborate celebrations at Kamal Ataturk Park in Banani.
Makeshift pandals at Kalabagan ground and Khamarbari have also emerged as major attractions for visitors in the capital. Large makeshift mandaps and eye-catching lighting displays are drawing crowds to the venues.
Maha Navami will be celebrated on Tuesday with religious fervour and enthusiasm. Devotees will gather at temples and mandaps to offer anjali as the day will feature major concluding worship rituals and the offering of bhog.
On Wednesday, Maha Dashami will be celebrated marking the farewell to Goddess Durga. Devotees will take the idols in processions to designated rivers, ponds and other water bodies for immersion, known as Bisarjan.

item.title: Real-time price information empowers vegetable farmers
item.description:
Thanks to mobile phones, rural vegetable growers now know the price of their produce in city markets. Farmers and small traders at the northern trading hub of Mohasthan, Bogra, say that they now come to the market with a realistic idea of prices.
Information about the prices of commodities flows freely thanks to mobile phones. Producers say this has enhanced their bargaining power though the prices ultimately depend on supply and demand.
Studies cited in development literature suggest that mobile connectivity significantly reduces the cost of searching for information. Vegetable growers now often use voice calls and SMS services to contact buyers before harvesting.
Md Aminul Islam (36), a farmer of Rahmotbala village in Bogra Sadar upazila, has grown radish, gourd, pumpkin and yard-long bean on one acre of land. On 2 October, he brought radish to Mohasthan vegetable market. "I knew the price of each maund (40 kilograms) was about Tk 1,000 three days ago, but today it has fallen to Tk 500-600 per maund. This is because of higher supply, and because the quality of this vegetable is sometimes not good when grown in hot weather,” he explained. "Farmers cannot unite to fix the price. Farmers and traders have mobile phones, so both can get information about supply and demand.”
Rabbi Molla (25), hailing from Utholi, Shibganj, who cultivated an early variety of cauliflower on about 50 decimals of land, said they get an idea of the likely prices of vegetables before harvesting by talking to other farmers and traders. "I sold some cauliflowers from the field. I come here (to Mohasthan) hoping for a higher price. Prices go up, prices go down. When the demand for vegetables in Dhaka or other cities increases, that is when wholesalers and traders offer us better prices," he pointed out.
Reading the price situation, many paikars (traders) buy seasonal vegetables from farmers and sell them to Mohasthan-based arotdars (wholesalers) who sell commodities in bulk to their counterparts in Dhaka and other cities. One such trader, Masum Islam (27) of Bichok, Shibganj, said, "I bought bitter gourd for Tk 1,600 per maund from farmers today, expecting to sell at Tk 1,800. I am struggling to get it because we don't know the exact price in advance," he said.
Wholesalers at Mohasthan buy vegetables depending on orders from wholesalers in cities, and also depending on the supply. Cucumbers, auburgines, sponge gourds, pumpkins, yard-long beans and olive are abundant at present. "The higher the supply, the higher the profitability for us. But when there is higher demand in Dhaka, the farmers also ask higher prices. Everybody keeps track of demand and supply, via phone or Facebook. Farmers now get a share of any price-hike," said Abdul Hamid Pramanik (48) of Lahiripara, Bogra, who has been operating in the wholesale market for about a decade.
The Mohasthan trading hub supplies vegetables to different cities. About 200 traders and 70 wholesalers (owners of trading houses) operate here. Al-Mamun (40) is the owner of one such arot (trading house). Maisha Traders. He observed that the use of mobile phones by farmers and small traders has revolutionized farming, ensuring farmers a fair price. "This has increased the competition in the business. You no longer see a huge difference between the price paid at the farm and the wholesale price. Of course any price-hike affects consumers, but farmers benefit," he added.
Hefzul Bari Fakir (40), a representative of Bishal Bhandar wholesale trading house in Mirpur, Dhaka, was at Mohasthan. He said, "I get orders with the likely price from Dhaka via mobile phone. I buy vegetables from farmers and small traders and transport them to Dhaka. Farmers have access to market information, and try to sell to whoever offers them a better price. If production falls, or if there is a problem in communication, vegetable prices go up."
Vegetables are perishable and spoil quickly. Experts have estimated that 30% of the vegetables harvested spoil before reaching consumers. As farmers and traders are now able to get price information quickly, this should help them to sell their vegetables quickly. It is hoped that this will reduce spoilage.

item.title: Rights and media advocates seek changes to Cyber Protection Act 2026
item.description:
Nineteen organizations working on rights and media issues have called for major changes to the proposed Cyber Protection Act, 2026, warning that several provisions could undermine freedom of expression, media independence and citizens’ rights.
The call came at a roundtable in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, on Sunday, where the organizations raised concerns over the proposed legislation.
At the discussion on proposed amendments to the law, speakers urged the government to remove offenses related to defamation, maligning, bullying, rumors and misinformation while retaining safeguards against arbitrary content restrictions.
The event was organized by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB), BRAC, the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST), Bangladesh Mahila Parishad and 15 other organizations.
Manab Zamin Editor and Newspaper Owners’ Association of Bangladesh (NOAB) President Matiur Rahman Chowdhury urged the government not to restrict the media, stressing that criticism of the government must be distinguished from cybercrime.
“While in power, governments often believe they need tough laws to silence criticism or ‘teach their opponents a lesson’. But they forget that once they lose power, a new government can use those same laws against them,” he said.
Matiur Rahman Chowdhury added: “Please do not tie our hands again. If you tie our hands, it will be to your own detriment. I will no longer be able to write for you. One day, you will have to come back to us.”
He said legislation was necessary to combat cybercrime, but criticism of the government was an essential part of a democratic society. Failure to distinguish between the two, he warned, would create further risks.
He also questioned a provision that could allow a newspaper or online news outlet to be shut down over an offense committed by an individual. Expressing concern over political influence in law enforcement, he warned that a phone call from a ruling party leader at the local level could lead to someone's arrest.
Questioning the proposed law's definition of misinformation, Chowdhury said a report could be labeled false or defamatory simply because someone disliked its contents. He called for clear criteria to determine what constituted intentional misinformation.
He also opposed granting mobile courts the authority to try journalists for cyber offenses, questioning whether such a measure was compatible with a democratic society.
Chowdhury urged the government to hold discussions across districts, consult people from all sections of society and ensure broader representation on committees involved in drafting the law.
TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman said the proposed legislation combined 3 distinct areas: cybercrime, cybersecurity and the exercise of human rights in cyberspace.
Bringing these areas under a single framework, he argued, risked prioritizing the concentration of state power over the protection of citizens' rights, particularly freedom of speech, expression and the media.
He said successive governments had continued a pattern of increasingly restrictive applications of cyber laws, raising concerns that human rights and freedom of expression were being criminalized.
Iftekharuzzaman also said 44 cases were filed under the law between March and September this year, accusing 101 people, of whom 64 had been arrested.
He questioned the composition of an expert committee formed by the government. While welcoming technical expertise in areas such as technology and engineering, he said the process must also reflect human rights concerns and include independent experts and representatives of broader sections of society.
He argued that tackling misinformation through restrictive criminal laws ran counter to international best practices, which emphasize cooperation with technology platforms, rights-based community standards, and greater transparency and accountability in algorithms.
The government had previously given verbal assurances that laws would not be misused against journalists, he said, but such assurances had failed to prevent abuses.
Fowzia Afroz, Bangladesh head of the Tech Global Institute, presented the findings and said Bangladesh's digital legal framework had undergone 6 changes over the past 2 decades, with another amendment now proposed, yet many of the same restrictive provisions continued to reappear.
Tracing the legal framework from the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006, and its Section 57, through the Digital Security Act, 2018, the Cyber Security Act, 2023, and subsequent cyber legislation, she said the pattern of restricting freedom of expression had persisted across successive governments.
Citing information published in newspapers, Afroz said 451 journalists were sued under the Digital Security Act between October 2018 and September 2023, including 255 over their reporting, while 97 were arrested.
She said provisions dealing with defamation, false information and social humiliation remained problematic because such terms could be vaguely defined and used to criminalize expression.
Afroz also raised concerns about making speech-related offenses non-bailable and allowing arrests without warrants.
“Twenty years later, we seem to have returned, to some extent, to where we were in 2006,” she said.
The organizations recommended deleting Section 25, which covers offenses related to defamation, maligning and bullying, and Section 26Ka, which addresses rumors and misinformation.
They called for retaining the safeguards, tribunal oversight and scope for challenging decisions under Sections 8(3) and 8(4), while amending Section 8(2) to remove vague grounds for content restrictions and additional content-blocking powers.
They also proposed amending Section 12 to restore the chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission, remove 5 additional government officials from the relevant committee and include independent experts.
The organizations recommended limiting Section 29 to ensure that speech-related offenses do not lead to licensing and registration penalties. They also called for removing the authority of mobile courts to try cyber offenses and deleting Section 46 to prevent the proposed speech-related offenses from being made cognizable.
The recommendations aim to ensure that efforts to protect cyberspace do not become a means of restricting legitimate expression or exposing journalists and citizens to arbitrary legal action.
The roundtable was moderated by Iftekharuzzaman. Other participants included Dhaka Union of Journalists President Md Shahidul Islam, former interim government press secretary and Daily Owad Editor Shafiqul Alam, Online Editors Forum Convener Sharifuzzaman Pintu, ABnews24 Editor Shahin Chowdhury and other representatives from the 19 organizations.

item.title: 4 members of a family from Jessore still missing after Cox’s Bazar resort fire
item.description:
Four members of a family from Jessore have remained missing following the fire at Tuptup Resto & Resort in Ukhiya of Cox’s Bazar on Saturday.
The missing family members are Nahidur Rahman, 41, son of Matiar Rahman of Mohonpur village under Manirampur Municipality in Jashore; his wife, Afsana Matin Tanji, 36; and their two children, Ruzaina Inaya, 7, and Sunaina Ihana, 3.
Family sources said Nahidur worked at an organization called Grand Power Limited in Shyamoli, Dhaka. He used to live with his wife and children in Shewrapara, Mirpur.
Nahidur’s elder brother, Zahidur Rahman Prince, said they learned from the resort booking bill that Nahidur had reserved a room at Tuptup Resto & Resort from October 16 to 18. He made the booking on October 11 and was scheduled to check out at 1pm on Sunday.
Zahidur said Nahidur told the family that he would travel to Cox’s Bazar on Friday.
After learning about the fire on Saturday, he repeatedly called his younger brother but could not reach him or any other family member.
“We still cannot confirm whether they are alive or dead. We are extremely worried about them,” he said.
Zahidur said Additional Superintendent of Police in Cox’s Bazar, Ahidur Rahman, informed him that a person named Nahid has been reported missing.
The police official also said DNA samples are being collected to identify the bodies, and the remaining four could possibly be Nahidur’s family members, he said.
