item.title: Prime Minister orders Ishraque to resign from Cabinet
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has instructed Ishraque Hossain, State Minister for Liberation War Affairs, to resign from the Cabinet following the controversy sparked by his participation in an anti-narcotics operation while carrying a firearm.

Several senior sources close to the government said the prime minister summoned Ishraque after a cabinet meeting at the Secretariat on Sunday afternoon and instructed him to resign.

However, as of the time this report was being written on Sunday night, no official statement on the matter had been obtained from any responsible government representative.

On Saturday, Ishraque Hossain took part in an anti-narcotics operation in Gandaria, in the capital, raising a firearm. Others accompanying him were also carrying weapons.

The video of the incident subsequently circulated on social media, triggering widespread debate and criticism.

The episode also caused unease and discontent within both the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the government. Against this backdrop, the prime minister instructed Ishraque to leave the Cabinet just a day after the incident.

According to people within the BNP and the government, there was no objection to the anti-narcotics initiative itself. However, they considered it unacceptable for a state minister to personally take part in an operation while carrying a firearm.

Questions were raised about why Ishraque had chosen to take up a weapon and join the operation himself rather than mobilise the administration to combat drugs.

The incident was particularly embarrassing for the government because the prime minister had been conducting surprise visits to various hospitals, educational institutions and government residential areas across the capital. These visits were intended to assess conditions and improve public services.

A member of the BNP Central Executive Committee, who spoke to Prothom Alo, also said the incident had ceased to be merely a personal matter for Ishraque and had embarrassed the prime minister and other Cabinet members. The Cabinet, the member added, would also have to bear responsibility for the conduct of a state minister. From Saturday morning until noon, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman made surprise visits to 13 locations across the capital. He issued instructions to the relevant officials regarding cleanliness and the quality of services at hospitals, educational institutions and government residential areas. At some locations, he also set deadlines for improvements. It was on the very day of these visits that Ishraque’s firearm-related controversy unfolded in the afternoon. Some party and government figures believe Ishraque’s actions substantially overshadowed the positive public discussion generated by the prime minister’s inspections. Against this backdrop, the order for Ishraque to resign is being viewed as a signal of the prime minister’s firm stance on the conduct and accountability of members of his government.

What Ishraaq did while holding a weapon

On Saturday afternoon, Ishraque Hossain, the Member of Parliament for the Dhaka-6 constituency, went on an anti-narcotics drive in the Dayaganj Ghunti Ghar railway gate area adjacent to Gandaria Railway Station in the capital. In a video published on his personal Facebook page, he is seen getting out of a vehicle, raising a firearm, and shouting, “Catch them, catch them, catch them…” Someone beside him can be heard saying, “I will shoot straight away.”

At this time, bodyguards accompanying the Minister of State ran to apprehend several individuals. One of them kicked a young man. Several people were heard saying, "Sir, I didn't do anything. I am a poor man, Sir." Another video shows the detained individuals being handed over to the police.

Present at the scene were Tofazzal Hossain and Lavlu, two bodyguards, appointed by the state minister, and an official state security officer. Tofazzal Hossain and Lavlu were also carrying weapons. Although the pistol in Ishraaq's hand was blurred out in certain parts of the video, the weapon was clearly visible in other sections. The identity of the individual who threatened to shoot has not been confirmed.

Following the incident, questions arose as to whether a Minister of State can conduct an anti-narcotics operation in such a manner while brandishing a firearm.

According to Clause 25 of the Ministry of Home Affairs' 2025 Policy on the Issuance, Renewal, and Use of Firearm Licences, although a licensed weapon may be carried and used for self-defence, it must not be displayed in a manner that creates fear or annoyance in others.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) is investigating the incident of Ishraque brandishing a weapon. At a press conference held today, Sunday, at the DMP Media Centre, Shafiqul Islam, the Chief of the Detective Branch, stated that the Deputy Commissioner of the Wari Division has been entrusted with the investigation.

He further said that it is being examined whether any violation of the law occurred during this incident. If evidence of a legal infraction is found, action will be taken against the individuals involved.

Claim of raising weapon in self-defence

Amid criticism regarding the firearm incident, Ishraque Hossain issued a statement on his verified Facebook page today, Sunday. In it, he claimed that he had gone there to participate in a social resistance programme against narcotics.

He stated that the programme was undertaken through a joint decision involving the police alongside local political and social leaders.

According to Ishraque, after receiving complaints regarding drug sales in various areas of Gandaria within the Dhaka-6 constituency, he had already been in discussions with law enforcement agencies. He had also taken initiatives to address manpower shortages and to establish a permanent police outpost near the drug dens. However, the issue remained unresolved.

In the statement, Ishraque claimed that prior to the drive, he learned that drug dealers might open fire from rooftops. Upon reaching the vicinity of a temporary drug den, a group of 30 to 35 individuals aggressively advanced towards their convoy while making a commotion. Fearing a potential attack and to ensure the safety of himself and others, he and his official security personnel briefly raised their weapons. Once the situation normalised, the weapons were put away.

Ishraque stated that the firearm in his hand was legal and licensed. He maintained that it was displayed purely in self-defence and claimed that no violation of the law had occurred.

In his statement, Ishraque further claimed that four to five temporary drug dens were demolished during the drive. Narcotics, weapons, cash, and stolen mobile phones were seized from the site. Six individuals were detained and handed over to the police. He alleged that several media outlets had presented a fragmented picture of the incident while ignoring these facts. The Minister of State also affirmed that anti-narcotics activities would continue.

However, questions remain as to whether there was prior coordination with the police before going to the scene. On Saturday, Masud Rana, Additional Deputy Commissioner of the Wari Division, told journalists that the Minister of State had not informed the police in advance, and that they only found out about the matter later. On Saturday, Ishraque also told the media that he asked the police to arrive 10 minutes after he reached the location.

Misti's resignation

Before Ishraque was directed to resign, Ferdousi Ahmed Misti, an MP from the BNP's reserved seats for women, had to step down following controversy surrounding the actions of individuals close to her.

On 25 September, an incident involving an attack, looting, and the demolition of a building occurred at the Radda Health Centre in Mirpur, Dhaka. In connection with this event, the names of several local BNP and Juba Dal figures known to be close to Misti surfaced. The incident created discomfort within both the government and the party, raising questions regarding Misti's political accountability, although she denied any personal involvement in the attack and vandalism.

Following directions from the Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman, Misti submitted her resignation letter to Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad on 1 October. Subsequently, the Parliament Secretariat declared her seat vacant.

Within two and a half weeks of Mishti's resignation, prime minister has now directed Minister of State Ishraque Hossain to leave the Cabinet following this firearm incident. In both instances, directions to resign came after actions that embarrassed both the party and the government.

item.title: Durga Puja’s core philosophy is standing against injustice, oppression: President
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Sunday said that standing up against injustice and oppression is the main philosophy of Durga Puja.

“Standing up against injustice, oppression, dishonesty, persecution and defeating them is the very core philosophy of Durga Puja,” he said while exchanging views with members of the Hindu community after visiting Ramna Temple on the occasion of Sharadiya Durgotsav- 2026.

Extending greetings to all on the occasion of Durga Puja, the President said, “Today’s event is one of the biggest celebrations for the people of the Sanatan faith. Not only in Bangladesh but across the world, Goddess Durga appeared when injustice, oppression, persecution and torture had descended upon people.”

“Demons had emerged repeatedly in this country, and the people of Bangladesh had defeated them,” he added.

Highlighting the history of Ramna Kali Temple, he said attempts were made to destroy it in 1971 and it was completely demolished in 1973.

“Those who spoke of secularism were responsible for this misdeed,” he noted.

The President said that in 2001, the Ramna Kali Temple was restored and rebuilt at the initiative of Babu Goyeshwar Chandra Roy under the direction of Begum Khaleda Zia.

“Since then, efforts have been made to restore the temple to its former heritage. I deeply commemorate late Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia with due respect for this,” he said.

He called upon all to remain united to preserve communal harmony in the country and said, “Bangladesh’s communal harmony was often misrepresented and subjected to misinformation.”

“We can say in a very firm and emphatic voice that I am not aware of any other place in the world where communal harmony exists as it does in Bangladesh,” he added.

The President further said that while violence and hatred were engulfing the world, the people of the Sanatan community in Bangladesh were able to celebrate their religious festival in an atmosphere of peace.

He assured that the present government would work sincerely to resolve the problems currently faced by followers of the Sanatan faith.

He wished the Durga Puja celebrations every success and thanked cultural performers who performed dances and songs on the occasion.

Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Hindu, Buddhist, Christian and Ethnic Minority Affairs Bijon Kanti Sarkar, Ramna Temple President Arpana Roy Das, and General Secretary Milton Baidya were present on the occasion.

During the programme, Ramna Temple member Subhash Chandra Das presented the President with a traditional uttariya.

item.title: Ishraque’s firearm controversy: Unease and discontent within BNP, govt
item.description:
Stepping out of his vehicle, he brandished a firearm and began shouting. Someone beside him was heard exclaiming, “I will shoot you dead.” This action by Ishraque Hossain, the State Minister for Liberation War Affairs, during an anti-narcotics drive, has sparked unease and discontent both within his own party, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), and inside the government.

Cabinet members and officials at the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) expressed embarrassment, questioning why a state minister felt compelled to take up arms and lead a raid himself instead of mobilising the administration to combat illicit drugs.

The incident occurred on the very day Prime Minister Tarique Rahman conducted visits across the capital, inspecting hospitals, educational institutions, and government residential areas.

Figures within the party and government believe that the positive momentum generated by the Prime Minister’s day-long inspections was largely overshadowed by Ishraque’s conduct.

A senior BNP leader noted that the entire Cabinet would have to share responsibility for such behaviour from a state minister.

Prothom Alo spoke with 10 individuals on condition of anonymity, including members of the BNP Central Executive Committee, ministers, and several PMO officials. While none objected to the necessity of anti-narcotics measures, all expressed concern over the state minister’s method of operation.

A member of the BNP Central Executive Committee told Prothom Alo that the matter had not remained merely an individual issue for Ishraque; it had embarrassed both the prime minister and fellow cabinet colleagues.

“The cabinet must take responsibility for such conduct by a state minister,” the leader stated.

Figures within the party and government believe that the positive momentum generated by the Prime Minister’s day-long inspections was largely overshadowed by Ishraque’s conduct.

Meanwhile, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into the armed raid. Speaking at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Sunday afternoon, Detective Branch (DB) Chief Shafiqul Islam announced that the Deputy Commissioner of the Wari Division had been entrusted with the probe, assuring that legal action would follow if any breach of the law is identified.

Ishraque Hossain, however, defended his actions as part of a “social resistance” against drugs.

In a statement issued today, Sunday, he claimed he had briefly brandished the weapon in self-defence due to fear of an imminent attack, adding that the firearm in question was legal and licensed.

What Ishraque was doing with firearm during the raid

The incident occurred on Saturday afternoon near the Dayaganj Ghanti Ghar railway gate, adjacent to Gandaria Railway Station in the capital.

Video footage of the event was published on Ishraque’s official Facebook page, showing him alighting from his car and shouting while brandishing a handgun. Someone beside him could be heard saying, “I will shoot you dead.”

State Minister Ishraque explains why he took part in anti-narcotics raid with firearms

Accompanied by his associates, they moved towards several individuals near the railway line to apprehend them, during which one of Ishraque’s bodyguards was seen kicking a youth.

This sequence of events drew strong objections from a top leader of the BNP’s Dhaka City South unit. Requesting anonymity, he told Prothom Alo that undertaking an armed anti-narcotics drive is not the duty of a Member of Parliament or a Minister.

Their role, he emphasised, is to assist the administration. Asking, “Why should anyone perform a function outside their jurisdiction?”, he added that the incident had damaged the image of both the party and the government.

Party and government insiders feel that despite good intentions, the state minister’s conduct rendered the effort controversial. Public discourse has shifted away from the necessity of eradicating drugs toward his brandishing of a weapon and the behaviour of the people who were with him.

Defending his initiative on Saturday, Ishraque cited complaints from local residents and the spread of narcotics in the area, pointing to limitations faced by law enforcement.

He maintained that he went there out of a sense of obligation and accountability to the public as their representative.

Nevertheless, party and government insiders feel that despite good intentions, the state minister’s conduct rendered the effort controversial. Public discourse has shifted away from the necessity of eradicating drugs toward his brandishing of a weapon and the behaviour of the people who were with him.

While the video posted on State Minister Ishraque Hossain’s Facebook page had the pistol blurred out, clear images of the firearm remained visible in certain segments of the clip.

Controversy on the day of the PMs inspection

Between 9:10 am and 1:41 pm on Saturday, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman toured various areas across the capital. Over nearly four and a half hours, he visited 13 locations—including hospitals, educational institutions, government quarters, and hawker-free footpaths in Mirpur-10—inspecting cleanliness and public services while issuing directives to the relevant authorities, setting deadlines ranging from seven days to two weeks for improvements.

Police order probe into State Minister Ishraque's use of firearms in anti-drug drive

A cabinet member who accompanied the prime minister during these visits told Prothom Alo on Saturday night that he felt the prime minister’s achievements throughout the day were ruined by Ishraque’s actions. He admitted that he personally felt embarrassed and annoyed.

An important government official echoed similar sentiments, stating via phone on Sunday morning that while Ishraque’s intentions against drugs were commendable, his reckless approach was concerning.

The official also noted that the state minister’s controversial actions had marred an otherwise excellent programme conducted by the prime minister.

The senior BNP executive committee member made a similar observation. He stated that the behaviour of a state minister had cast a shadow over the prime minister’s efforts and embarrassed the entire cabinet amidst ongoing initiatives to establish government accountability.

Ishraque’s defense

Amid mounting criticism, Ishraque issued a statement on Sunday claiming that as they approached a temporary drug den, a group of 30 to 35 individuals advanced aggressively toward their motorcade shouting threats. Sensing an imminent attack, he and his official security members briefly raised their weapons strictly for self-defence, lowering them once the situation normalised.

The leader, who maintains regular contact with the diplomatic community, spoke on condition of anonymity, stating he believed the photos and videos circulating in media and on social platforms had already caught the attention of foreign embassies in Dhaka.

In his statement, the state minister highlighted previous initiatives undertaken to curb the drug trade locally, including steps to set up a permanent police outpost and address manpower shortages.

He maintained that he participated in the social resistance programme based on prior discussions with the police as well as local political and civic leaders.

However, coordination with law enforcement prior to arriving at the scene remains unclear. Although Ishraque claimed to have held prior discussions with the police, he told news media on Saturday that he had called for police support 10 minutes after reaching the location.

Masud Rana, Additional Deputy Commissioner of the DMP’s Wari Division, informed newspersons on Saturday that the state minister had not notified the police in advance and that they learned of the matter only after the event.

Consequently, despite broad agreement on anti-narcotics initiatives, questions persist over whether proper coordination took place prior to this specific raid.

Questions have also arisen regarding the manner in which the firearm was displayed, in addition to its legality. Section 25 of the Ministry of Home Affairs’ 2025 Guidelines on Firearms Licensing, Renewal, and Usage stipulates that while licensed weapons may be carried for self-defence, they must not be displayed in a manner that causes alarm or annoyance to others.

The police investigation will examine whether any legal violations occurred during the incident. DB Chief Shafiqul Islam affirmed that appropriate legal measures would be enforced based on the probe’s findings.

State Minister Ishraque joins anti-drug drive with firearm, faces questions over its use

For figures within the party and government, however, the incident is both about legal issues and the expected standards of conduct for a cabinet member. They stressed that if there are administrative shortcomings in combating drug trafficking, a state minister has the authority to intervene administratively. Taking up arms to personally conduct a raid not only highlights administrative gaps but also invites serious questions regarding his role.

Concerns over diplomatic image

Ishraque is also a member of the BNP’s International Affairs Committee. A prominent leader of the BNP Central Executive Committee expressed deep concern over the impression these images and videos of an armed raid might create among foreign diplomats regarding the party and the government.

The leader, who maintains regular contact with the diplomatic community, spoke on condition of anonymity, stating he believed the photos and videos circulating in media and on social platforms had already caught the attention of foreign embassies in Dhaka. The member voiced concern that diplomats would view such conduct by a cabinet member in a highly negative light.

Meanwhile, on social media, calls for Ishraque’s removal from the cabinet have emerged alongside widespread criticism. In response, the state minister posted an update on his Facebook page Saturday evening, declaring that operations would continue until the Dhaka-6 constituency is completely freed from drugs, adding that no quarter would be given even if members of his own party were involved in illicit trades.

Nonetheless, insiders within the party and government emphasise that taking a firm stance against narcotics and taking law enforcement duties into one’s own hands are entirely distinct matters.

While the police investigation will determine the legal aspects of the weapon display, concerned individuals maintain that the state minister’s actions have damaged the image of both the party and the government, with several expecting disciplinary action to follow.

item.title: Ishraque: Will use bamboo sticks instead of firearms to destroy drug dens
item.description:
Following criticism over a video showing him carrying a pistol during an anti-drug drive in Dhaka, State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has said he will use bamboo sticks instead of firearms to destroy drug dens.
In a post on his verified Facebook account on Sunday night, October 18, he criticized media coverage of the drive and said drug dens would be razed.
“Some renowned media outlets have panels of renowned lawyers through whom they can seek clear explanations of the law, and I believe they practise this. Despite knowing and understanding everything, the way they are reporting makes it seem that they were exclusive suppliers of drugs in the ‘ghuntighor’. That is why they are behaving like wild animals after my drive. Wait and see. All drug dens (which may be financing these papers) will be levelled to the ground,” he wrote.
“I had a legally licensed firearm for my personal security. From now on, I will destroy these dens with bamboo sticks. The police will stand and watch, and the offenders will be arrested in front of a magistrate and taken away. The 16 aspects of the anti-drug struggle will be fulfilled, insha’Allah,” he added.
On Saturday, Ishraque Hossain, the member of parliament for Dhaka-6, took part in an anti-drug drive near the Gandaria railway line.
A video shared on Facebook showed him carrying a hand microphone and a pistol as he chased people, pulled back the pistol’s slide and pointed it at them while ordering them to stop. Others accompanying him were also seen carrying firearms.
The video raised questions about whether a licensed personal firearm could be displayed in this manner and whether an elected representative could personally conduct an armed anti-drug drive.
On Sunday, Detective Branch (DB) chief and Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Additional Commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam said the relevant deputy commissioner had been asked to review the incident locally and submit a report. He said police would take action under the law if any violation was found.
Ishraque Hossain claimed that 30–35 people had approached his convoy aggressively during a social anti-drug resistance program. He said he and his security personnel had briefly raised their firearms to prevent a possible attack.
He also claimed that, with assistance from local police, they had removed 4–5 drug dens, recovered drugs and weapons, and detained 6 people before handing them over to the police.

item.title: Indian air ambulance lands in Dhaka after door opens mid-air; patient dies
item.description:
An air ambulance traveling from Agartala, India, to Kolkata made an emergency landing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Sunday afternoon after its door suddenly opened mid-air. An ill woman aboard the aircraft later died, according to an airport source.
After the aircraft landed in Dhaka, the patient, identified as Anjana Bhowmik, was taken to Kurmitola Hospital, where doctors declared her dead, the source said.
Bhowmik was an Indian national. She was accompanied by physician Firoz Khan, paramedic Azim Khan and 2 companions, Santa Bhowmik and Deep Jyoti Mishra. The air ambulance's passenger list identified all of them as Indian nationals.
The air ambulance was operated by SKB Infracon Private Limited. The aircraft was a C90A model with registration number VT-HYA and was traveling from Agartala to Kolkata.
Captain Punya Anup was the pilot-in-command, while Captain Tanuj Sharma was the co-pilot. A total of 7 people, including the 2 pilots, were aboard the aircraft.

item.title: 118 flights cancelled at Dhaka airport in 7 days
item.description:
A total of 118 flights at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka were canceled over the past 7 days due to restrictions on flight operations at Riyadh and Dammam airports in Saudi Arabia, affecting 18,362 passengers.
According to information sent by the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) on Sunday, October 18, 52 of the canceled flights were direct flights and 66 were transit flights.
Of the canceled direct flights, 19 were operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 by US-Bangla Airlines, 13 by Saudia Airlines and 10 by Riyadh Air.
Meanwhile, the canceled transit flights included 23 operated by IndiGo, 7 by SalamAir, 1 by EgyptAir, 14 by Emirates Airlines, 9 by Qatar Airways, 6 by flydubai and 6 by Air India.

item.title: 'I had no intention of killing him, I am not remorseful’
item.description:
The prime accused in the case filed over the lynching of Wahiduzzaman Shamim in Debhata, Satkhira, Fazlul Haque Ameni, has said he had no intention of killing the victim and that the incident happened accidentally, adding that he was not remorseful.
He made the comments while responding to questions from journalists following his arrest.
Ameni was arrested around 11pm on Saturday from a relative’s house in Faridpur village of Kaliganj upazila in Satkhira. Members of Debhata Circle, Kaliganj police station, Debhata police station and Special Response Battalion (SRB)-6 conducted a joint operation to arrest him.
He was handed over to Satkhira Sadar police station on Sunday afternoon. Police sent him to court around 4pm.
Responding to journalists while being handed over to police, Ameni said: “I am a criminal in the eyes of the law. But you have seen what I did on social media. Almighty Allah will deliver the proper judgment. However, I had no intention of beating him to death. It happened accidentally.”
Asked whether he regretted Shamim’s death, Ameni said: “No, I am not remorseful about this. We did not initially realize how much of an atheist he was. Later, when atheists from different countries called me on my phone and threatened me, I became certain that he was actually an atheist.”
Debhata police station Officer-in-Charge HM Shaheen said Ameni had admitted to his involvement in the killing.
He said Ameni had informed police that he would make a confessional statement before a court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. Police therefore believe there is no need to take him into remand, the OC added.
According to the case statement, an audio recording of a conversation between Shamim, 38, and his wife was circulated on Facebook on October 12. After allegations that the recording contained derogatory remarks about religion, locals became agitated and attacked Shamim’s house.
The following afternoon, Shamim was allegedly dragged out of a rural doctor’s chamber at a local market and beaten while receiving treatment.
Police rescued him and admitted him to Debhata Upazila Health Complex. Later that night, around 8:30pm, a group allegedly led by Fazlul Haque Ameni attacked the hospital, took Shamim away and assaulted him again.
Shamim died while being taken to Satkhira Medical College Hospital.
His elder brother Abdul Jalil later filed a murder case with Debhata Police Station, naming 10 people and accusing 200–250 unidentified individuals. Ameni was named the prime accused.

item.title: Teen gang leader sent to jail after surrender in extortion case
item.description:
A listed criminal who eluded police during an operation earlier this month has surrendered to a court in Chittagong in an extortion case, with the court rejecting his bail petition and ordering him sent to jail.
Wakil Hossain alias Boga, a leader of a “teen gang” listed by Chittagong Metropolitan Police, surrendered on Sunday.
Wakil surrendered and sought bail before the court of Chittagong Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Mahidul Islam on Sunday afternoon. After the hearing, the court rejected his application and ordered his detention in jail.
Hasan Iqbal Chowdhury, deputy commissioner (prosecution) of CMP, confirmed the information to Dhaka Tribune. He said Wakil Hossain Boga had surrendered and sought bail in an extortion case, but the court ordered him sent to jail after the hearing.
Wakil was a former joint convener of the city unit of Swechchhasebak Dal. He was expelled from the party on June 8 over allegations of activities contrary to party discipline.
He faces 23 cases involving allegations including murder, arms, drugs, extortion and land grabbing. Police claim that Wakil controlled several teen gangs and used his political influence to carry out criminal activities.
On October 6, police went to the Chittagong City Corporation building in the city's Tigerpass area after receiving information that Wakil was there. However, they failed to find him during the operation.
The following day, Chittagong City Corporation Mayor Shahadat Hossain said Wakil had not been inside the city corporation building and that his 2 brothers had come to meet him. At the time, the mayor described Wakil as a “July warrior” rather than a criminal and made several allegations against then Khulshi police station Officer-in-Charge Abdur Rahim.
Abdur Rahim was subsequently removed from Khulshi police station and transferred to the metropolitan police's CTSB branch. The following day, he was transferred from Chittagong to the Khulna Police Training Centre.

item.title: 17 dead, 25 hurt in stampede at India religious gathering
item.description:
At least 17 people were killed and two dozen more injured Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that was likely caused by sudden rainfall during a Hindu religious gathering, officials said.
West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 others were injured outside a pavilion “in a stampede” at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata.
“Six bodies have so far been identified,” Adhikari said.
A senior police official at the scene told AFP an announcement caused “commotion” after it started raining at night and the “crowd waiting outside the pandal (pavilion) was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.”
Deadly crowd incidents are a frequent occurrence at Indian mass events, such as religious festivals, due to poor management and safety lapses.
Last year, a stampede at India's Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others, and 11 fans were crushed to death in Bengaluru during celebrations for the local cricket team's first Indian Premier League title.
The same year, 36 people were killed after a stampede broke out at a campaign rally of a popular actor-turned-politician in southern Tamil Nadu state.
In 2024, 121 people were killed in northern Uttar Pradesh state during a Hindu religious gathering.

item.title: Family members provide DNA samples to identify Cox’s Bazar fire victims
item.description:
Family members of victims killed in a fire at Cox’s Bazar’s TUPTUP Resto & Resort provided DNA samples to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) in Dhaka on Sunday to help identify their remains.
Of the 10 tourists killed in the fire, six were members of the same extended family — four girls and two boys who were cousins. Their bodies were severely burnt, making identification difficult.
A CID media official confirmed that DNA samples were collected from six relatives on Sunday, while another was expected to provide a sample on Monday.
Zeyadul Kabir travelled from Barguna to Dhaka to provide samples to identify the remains of his son, Mohammad Nafis Istehami, and daughter, Fariha Kabir. He was accompanied by Md Mamunur Rashid, the father of Ishrat Jahan Maliha and Layla Jahan.
Md Nur-e-Alam provided a sample to identify the remains of his seven-year-old son, Faizan Noor, while Shahjahan gave a sample for his daughter, Mithila Mehezabeen Arvi.
Zeyadul Kabir, Mamunur Rashid and Shahjahan are brothers-in-law, while Nur-e-Alam is Zeyadul Kabir’s son-in-law. Speaking to reporters after providing his sample at the CID office, Zeyadul said the remains of six members of their family had yet to be identified as they were severely burnt.
“We still do not know when their remains will be identified. Officials have assured us that they will use DNA testing to identify the bodies and hand them over to us as soon as possible, but they could not say how long it would take,” he said, his voice breaking.
He urged the authorities to complete the identification process and return the remains to the family as quickly as possible. “We cannot bring our children back, but we want their remains returned to us as soon as possible after all necessary procedures are completed,” he said.

item.title: Jamaat: Ishraque brandishing of firearm signals a reign of terror
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Sunday condemned State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain for brandishing a firearm during an anti-drug drive in Dhaka’s Gandaria area, saying the incident signals a reign of terror.
In a statement, Jamaat Central Publicity and Media Department Secretary Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair said Ishraque, also a lawmaker from Dhaka-6, was seen raising a pistol during the drive on Saturday afternoon. “The incident signals a reign of terror,” he said.
Drug abuse has increased, and the law and order situation has deteriorated since the BNP government assumed office.
He said ministers, state ministers and other government officials launched various activities to divert public attention from their failures.
As part of these activities, he said, Ishraque’s action during the anti-drug drive is an expression of a reign of terror.
Referring to the country’s existing arms laws, the Jamaat leader said no person could use a licensed firearm to create public panic except for personal security.
He said it is undesirable, unlawful and unacceptable for a state minister to take the law into his own hands, brandish a firearm and create fear among people despite having the law enforcement agencies and the administration.
He also criticized what he described as the aggressive role of the minister’s bodyguards.
Zubair called for action by the responsible authorities of the government to address the incident and said the minister concerned should take an active role in mobilizing law enforcement agencies.
He said Ishraque Hossain’s act of uploading videos of his own unlawful activities to the social media platform Facebook—with the clear intent to instill fear among the people and establish a reign of terror—is unacceptable.
The Jamaat leader said the state minister had violated his oath through such an action, which could further encourage criminals.

item.title: BGB seizes smuggled goods worth Tk957 crore in Sarail region
item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has seized drugs and smuggled goods worth Tk957.13 crore during operations by 13 battalions under its Sarail region up to October 15 this year, detaining 333 people and taking legal action against them.
Lieutenant Colonel Md Hasibul Islam, commanding officer of Feni Battalion (4 BGB), disclosed the information at a press briefing organised by the battalion on Sunday.
The briefing highlighted operations along the border, seizures of drugs and smuggled goods, and measures to strengthen border security.
According to BGB, the seized items included 340,815 yaba pills, 14,967kg of cannabis, 63,575 bottles of foreign liquor, 16,880 bottles of beer, and Phensedyl and Eskuf syrups. The force also seized 432,510 sexual stimulant tablets and 210 litres of locally brewed liquor, reports Bangla Tribune.
Other recoveries included 11 pistols, seven air guns, five pipe guns, 62 rounds of ammunition, 19kg of high explosives, 117 detonators and 77 metres of detonator wire.
To protect natural resources, BGB also seized 16,800 cubic feet of stone and 8,200 cubic feet of sand.
Officials said 211 border outposts (BOPs) under 13 battalions across four sectors of the Sarail region were conducting surveillance and patrols along nearly 1,204km of border.
Meanwhile, five platoons of BGB personnel have been deployed to ensure security at 18 Durga Puja venues within Feni Battalion's area of responsibility. A base camp has also been set up at Buxmahmood High School in Parshuram.
Security measures include regular patrols, intelligence surveillance and coordination with the local administration and police.
Lieutenant Colonel Hasibul Islam said BGB operations would continue to protect the country's sovereignty and borders, prevent drug trafficking and smuggling, and ensure the safety and welfare of border residents.
He urged the public to avoid spreading rumours and report suspicious information to law enforcement agencies to help maintain a peaceful atmosphere during Durga Puja.

item.title: Passenger held with Tk1.2C worth of gold at Chittagong airport
item.description:
A passenger arriving from Abu Dhabi was arrested at Shah Amanat International Airport in Chittagong on Sunday after 566 grams of gold, worth an estimated Tk1.2 crore, were recovered from his luggage.
The gold was concealed inside a non-stick pan, a vegetable blender and a dish rack, according to airport authorities.
The passenger, Mohammad Kamrul Islam, is a resident of Banshkhali upazila in Chittagong. A case has been filed against him with Patenga police station on charges of smuggling gold.
Mohammad Ibrahim Khalil, public relations officer of Shah Amanat International Airport, said Kamrul arrived in Chittagong on a US-Bangla Airlines flight from Abu Dhabi.
During a search at the customs hall, officials found his movements suspicious and proceeded to inspect his luggage, he said.
The search was conducted under the joint supervision of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI), the National Security Intelligence (NSI) and Customs Intelligence personnel stationed at the airport.
Four gold bars weighing a total of 466 grams were recovered from inside the non-stick pan, stainless steel vegetable blender and dish rack. A gold bangle weighing 100 grams was also found in his possession.
The airport authorities estimated the market value of the recovered gold at Tk1.2 crore.
According to a statement from the airport’s public relations department, the seized gold was handed over to airport customs. Arrangements were under way to hand Kamrul over to Patenga police.

item.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats, beat French mayor
item.description:
Israeli settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats in the West Bank and beat up a visiting French mayor on Saturday, witnesses said, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing “crisis” in the territory a day after an American photojournalist was injured in a brutal attack.
Violence is surging ahead of bitterly fought October 27 elections, coinciding with Palestinians’ annual olive harvest which has been repeatedly disrupted by Israeli settlers as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks to shore up his pro-settlement right-wing base.
On Saturday, the 78-year-old mayor said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France and kicked and hit him with iron bars as he joined Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank alongside top French and Belgian representatives in Jerusalem and Polish diplomats.
“I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, told AFP after he was attacked.
“The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said.
“For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.”
Baudoux, who was wearing a sash with the French tricolour, was seen collapsed on the side of the car after the attack but he did not need hospital care.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said in a statement that Israel must “urgently halt criminal violence” and arrest those responsible for attacking Baudoux, while his Belgian counterpart issued a similar call.
The attack came just one day after settlers beat up Heidi Levine, an American photographer for The Washington Post, who was in a moderate condition on Saturday after suffering broken vertebrae.
“We’re very disturbed by those images and what we’re seeing,” Rubio told reporters Saturday, adding that US President Donald Trump “does not want to see friction or anything -- a crisis going on in the West Bank.”
Trump “doesn’t want to see a new spark,” Rubio added.
Israel’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on the diplomats and Israeli police promised to open an investigation.
But Netanyahu, who is seeking to shore up support from the fiercely pro-settlement far-right in this month’s election, instead alleged a “smear” campaign against settlers.
Netanyahu said the diplomats should have coordinated their movements with the Israeli military and pointed out that Baudoux is a communist known for supporting the Palestinian cause.
His main rival in the elections, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, slammed Netanyahu over the violence, saying it was “burning away the little legitimacy the State of Israel still possesses”.
The attacks are “Jewish terrorism, under the auspices of the Israeli government”, Eisenkot said.
President Isaac Herzog, who holds a mostly ceremonial role, called Levine in hospital on Saturday, saying the attack was “outrageous and shocking” and weighed on his conscience.
US Ambassador Mike Huckabee said the beating was “a despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards”, and demanded Israel prosecute and jail the assailants.
Baudoux, the mayor, said he had come to the town of Taybeh, a Christian stronghold, along with his local pastor from France to sign a goodwill agreement.
He was attacked as he joined the harvest as a symbolic gesture with Palestinians, for whom olives are an important cultural symbol.
Rubio also acknowledged the season, and added “there are other instances we’ve heard complaints about.”
Extremist Israelis have issued calls to stop the Palestinians’ annual harvest after months of attacks in which settlers have stolen land and property. There has also been violence against Israelis, with a Palestinian fatally shooting a settler last month.
Bashar Fawadleh, a priest in Taybeh, said settlers also attacked the harvest and snatched olives before beating the mayor.
“One person was hit in the head and needed stitches. They also beat up an older lady in her 70s after insulting her,” the pastor told AFP.
The West Bank violence has shocked much of the world, with Britain spearheading economic sanctions that led Israel to close the British consulate in Jerusalem.
Israel Gantz, head of an umbrella settler group, blamed recent incidents on “groups of provocateurs and terrorists” but implicitly acknowledged some Israelis’ responsibility.
Settlers also beat up AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh earlier this month, as he covered the olive harvest tensions, fracturing several of his ribs and stealing his camera.
Netanyahu’s government has ramped up approval of West Bank settlements, which are illegal under international law.
About 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank, which Israel seized in 1967, alongside three million Palestinians.

item.title: Japan to launch historic round-trip mission to Mars moon
item.description:
Japanese scientists are readying a mission to Mars’s moons to retrieve samples that could help unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth, in what aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region.
The unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe, a collaboration with US and European space agencies as well as numerous universities and tech companies, could also help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration.
The flagship H3 rocket carrying the MMX is set to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center Tuesday at 4:41 am, according to the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA).
“Being able to be involved in such a grand mission is incredibly exciting,” Makoto Arita, project manager of JAXA’s H3 rocket team, told reporters two days before the launch.
The spacecraft will arrive near Mars around August next year, where it will orbit one of its moons, Phobos, before landing and collecting at least 10 grams of material from the surface during three years of operating within the Martian sphere.
A rover dubbed IDEFIX -- the French name for the comic hero Asterix’s dog -- will first conduct surface observations aimed at ensuring a safe landing.
“The sampling (from) Phobos is of course the world’s first, but it means... this is the first-round trip to the Martian system,” MMX’s project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu told AFP.
JAXA said the mission will also explore the possibility of using Phobos as a “natural space station” by establishing the requirements for a round trip to Mars -- something “essential for crewed Mars exploration”.
It will also observe the Red Planet’s moon Deimos, although it will not land on it, before returning to Earth.
JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born.
One theory for the origin of the Martian moons -- the “giant impact” hypothesis -- is that they formed after a celestial body collided with Mars.
The “capture” hypothesis, meanwhile, postulates that the moons are asteroids captured by Mars’s gravity.
Determining which theory is correct will help reveal “how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets”, JAXA said, referring to the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun -- Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
“MMX will shed light on the transport mechanisms that delivered water, volatiles, and organic compounds from the outer Solar System to the inner rocky planet region -- processes that may have played a key role in making these worlds habitable,” said Patrick Michel, a French astrophysicist working on IDEFIX.
“If Phobos and Deimos are indeed remnants of these early delivery systems, they may hold clues to the origins of life itself, or, to be more correct, to the transport of the materials that were key to the emergence of life on rocky planets,” he told AFP.
MMX is a collaboration with France’s National Centre for Space Studies (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR), NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA), and about 20 universities and tech companies.
The development of the spacecraft’s landing legs was particularly difficult, as gravity on Phobos is extremely weak, JAXA scientists say.
Japan’s unmanned Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM) -- the “Moon Sniper” -- tipped over after touching down on Earth’s Moon in 2024, but still transmitted data and survived several two-week lunar nights.
Japan also has experience in bringing back samples from space, including JAXA’s unmanned Hayabusa-2, which returned 5.4 grams of rock and dust collected from an asteroid several hundred million kilometres from Earth in 2020.
On the upcoming mission “we have to travel very close to Mars and return”, which means escaping the planet’s heavy gravity, Kawakatsu told reporters.
Phobos orbits about 6,000 kilometres above the Martian surface.
“Going deep into what we call the ‘gravity well’ is difficult,” Kawakatsu said.
US and Chinese space agencies have been racing to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth.
NASA’s Perseverance rover, which has been roaming the Red Planet since 2021, has already collected samples.
The mission, however, was effectively cancelled by the administration of President Donald Trump following a vote by the US Congress in January.
China, meanwhile, has announced its Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and hopes to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 -- potentially before the MMX’s return.
JAXA scientists say sand and rocks from Phobos may offer a wider variety of samples than those on the planet itself, especially if it was formed by a collision between a celestial body and Mars.

item.title: EU ‘strongly condemns’ settler attack on delegation in West Bank
item.description:
The European Union said Sunday that it “strongly condemns” an attack the previous day by a group of Israeli settlers on visiting European diplomats.
“The EU strongly condemns the latest attacks by violent settlers in the West Bank, including on European diplomats,” the foreign service said in a communique.
The communique also urged “full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists.
“We urge Israel to fully abide by International Humanitarian and Human Rights Law, and to cease the expansion of settlements,” the statement concluded.
Saturday saw Israeli settlers attack a convoy of European diplomats in the West Bank and beat up a visiting French mayor, witnesses said, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing “crisis” in the territory a day after an American photojournalist was injured in a brutal attack.
Violence is surging ahead of bitterly fought October 27 elections in Israel, coinciding with an olive harvest repeatedly disrupted by Israeli settlers as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks to shore up his pro-settlement right-wing base.
On Saturday, 78-year-old Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France and kicked and hit him with iron bars.
“I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Baudoux told AFP after he and visiting EU representatives were attacked.
“The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Israel must “urgently halt criminal violence” and arrest those responsible while his Belgian counterpart issued a similar call.
